 Judgment

(PER: THE HON'BLE MR. JUSTICE H.T.NARENDRA PRASAD)
1.

This appeal under Section 173(1) of the Motor Vehicles Act, 1988 (hereinafter referred to as 'the Act', for short) has been filed by the insurance company challenging the judgment and award dated 10.09.2012 passed by the learned III Additional Senior Civil Judge and Addl. MACT, Dharwad, in MVC No.182/2009.
2.

entities.text: III Additional Senior Civil Judge and Addl. MACT, Dharwad
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text:
Facts giving rise to the filing of the appeal briefly stated are that, on 24.12.2008 Ramappa,
husband of petitioner No.1 and son of petitioner Nos.2 and 3, was riding his cycle from Chikkamalligawad to Bevoor, at that time, an ambassador car bearing registration No.KA.25/M- 3099 came from Dharwad towards Belgaum in a rash and negligent manner and dashed to the cycle of Ramappa due to which, he sustained grievous injuries and died on the NC: 2024:KHC-D:18002 way to KIMS Hospital.
Hence, the claimants filed a petition under Section 166 of the Act seeking compensation.
3. Upon service of notice, respondent Nos.1 and 2 appeared through their counsel.
Though sufficient time was granted, respondent No.1 did not file any objections.
Respondent No.2 filed objections denying the averments made in the claim petition.

sentences.text: On the basis of the pleadings of the parties, the Claims Tribunal framed the issues and thereafter recorded the evidence.
The Tribunal, by impugned judgment and award has partly allowed the petition awarding compensation of Rs.10,18,000/- with interest at 8% per annum from the date of petition till the date of payment.
Being aggrieved, present appeal has been filed by insurance company seeking reduction in the compensation as awarded by the Tribunal.
The learned counsel appearing for the insurance company contended that considering the age and avocation of the deceased, the over all compensation awarded by the Tribunal is on the higher side.

Secondly he has contended that, in view of judgment of this Court in MS.JOYEETA BOSE AND OTHERS -V- VENKATESHAN.V AND OTHERS (MFA 5896/2018 and connected matters disposed of on 24.8.2020), interest at 6% has to be awarded but the Tribunal has awarded interest on the compensation at 8% per annum, which is on the higher side.

entities.text: MS.JOYEETA BOSE AND OTHERS -V- VENKATESHAN.V AND OTHERS (MFA 5896/2018
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Hence, he sought for allowing the appeal.

6. Learned counsel appearing for the claimants has contended that considering the age and avocation of the deceased and evidence of the parties, the Tribunal has awarded just and reasonable compensation and the same does not call for interference.
Hence, he sought for dismissal of the appeal.
Heard the learned counsel for the parties and perused the impugned judgment and award.
8. It is not in dispute that Ramappa died in a road traffic accident occurred on 24.12.2008 due to rash and negligent driving by the driver of the car.
At the time of the accident, the deceased was aged about 25 years.
Considering the age and avocation of the deceased, the Tribunal has awarded just and reasonable compensation.

So far as interest is concerned, the Tribunal has awarded interest at the rate of 8% per annum which is on the higher side and the same has to be scaled down to 6%
per annum in view of the judgment of this Court in MS.JOYEETA BOSE (supra).
To that extent, the appeal deserves to be allowed.
Hence, the following order.
Accordingly, the appeal is allowed in part.
The judgment and award dated 10.09.2012 passed by the learned III Additional Senior Civil Judge and Addl. MACT, Dharwad, in MVC No.182/2009 is confirmed.

entities.text: Additional Senior Civil Judge and Addl. MACT, Dharwad
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text: However the NC: 2024:KHC-D:18002 rate of interest on the compensation amount is reduced to 6% per annum.

Insurance company is directed to deposit the entire compensation amount with interest at 6% per annum from the date of petition till the date of deposit within six weeks from the date of receipt of certified copy of this judgment.
The compensation of Rs.10,18,000/- awarded by the Tribunal is just and reasonable.
The registry is directed to transfer the amount in deposit to the Tribunal forthwith.
